author: WP18
summary: Updated-for-d6e9ff05 chapter on building Windows binaries on Linux: the MinGW toolchain file, target-built vendored SDL, runtime DLL staging, CTest emulator wiring for PE files and the separate native-MSVC lane. Mostly current; the claim that no Apple toolchain file exists is stale (ios.cmake) and one paragraph describes an audited machine's cache. Configuring CNA already covered the toolchain fallback and emulator chain; staging helpers, the dynamic-runtime reason, registration differences and the evidence tiers are now on a new deep dive.

concepts.text: The Windows loop starts on Linux in independent steps (select the MinGW target, build SDL for it, link a PE, stage its DLLs, run through the right Wine wrapper), each with its own failure mode, so a successful compile is not yet a runnable Windows program.
tokens: The route in five independent steps

concepts.text: mingw-w64.cmake sets Windows/x86_64, picks x86_64-w64-mingw32 or falls back to i686-w64-mingw32, sets the C, C++ and windres compilers, and keeps program lookup on the host while confining libraries, headers and packages to /usr/<triple>.
The i686 fallback leaves CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR at x86_64, so it rescues compiler discovery but is not a self-consistent 32-bit lane where processor-keyed caches or ABI checks matter.

The claim that CNA owns no Android, Emscripten or Apple toolchain file is stale: the tree has exactly two toolchain files, mingw-w64.cmake and ios.cmake; Android uses the NDK file and the web uses emcmake.

concepts.section: Vendored SDL is built for the target, not reused from the host
concepts.text: cna_configure_vendored_sdl() runs a nested configure, build and install of SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer that forwards the parent toolchain, so a MinGW tree gets Windows DLLs and import libraries instead of the host's SDL.

concepts.section: Vendored SDL is built for the target, not reused from the host
concepts.text: The persistent SDL install is keyed by system and processor (.sdl-prebuilt-Windows-x86_64 beside .sdl-prebuilt-Linux-x86_64), plus Apple deployment and Wayland suffixes and separate single-threaded and pthread Emscripten roots, and a fingerprint of sources, patches and configure arguments triggers a rebuild.
concepts.note: Extended/corrected: the web has two roots and rebuilds are fingerprint-driven.

concepts.section: Vendored SDL is built for the target, not reused from the host
concepts.text: An audited machine held only the Linux and Windows caches, and the Windows one contained GNU import libraries (libSDL3.dll.a) rather than MSVC .lib/.pdb files, which the older text used as direct evidence of cross-compilation.
concepts.note: Observation of one development machine’s working tree, not a property of the source; not reproducible from TARGET.

concepts.section: Vendored SDL is built for the target, not reused from the host
concepts.text: Configure-time dependency builds make the first configure heavier and stateful but keep the target explicit; a cache built under one ABI must be regenerated under the intended toolchain, never renamed into place.
tokens: must never be renamed into another's place

concepts.section: Runtime staging is part of a successful build
concepts.text: A PE linked against an import library needs the DLL beside it at run time; cna_copy_sdl_runtime copies the SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer DLLs next to each Windows target.

concepts.section: Runtime staging is part of a successful build
concepts.text: MinGW test executables link libgcc and libstdc++ statically and stage only libwinpthread-1.dll; application targets with large RTTI graphs use the dynamic runtime and cna_copy_mingw_cxx_runtime stages the SEH/DW2/SJLJ unwinder, libstdc++-6.dll and the threading DLL (the standalone platform harness does so because GCC 13's static libstdc++ duplicates type_info::operator==).

concepts.section: Runtime staging is part of a successful build
concepts.text: Each helper asks the compiler for the runtime file (-print-file-name) and falls back to its bin directory; a miss is only a configure warning, so verification must start or inspect the staged directory rather than stop at 'target built'.

concepts.section: Runtime staging is part of a successful build
concepts.text: Renderer-specific runtime pieces (Direct3D translators, Direct2D's Wine runtime) are not staged by the generic MinGW helpers; they come from the Wine prefix.

concepts.section: CTest must know that PE files are not host executables
concepts.text: GoogleTest PRE_TEST discovery executes CnaTests.exe, so a cross tree sets CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR on CnaTests to the matching Wine wrapper for DIRECTX9, DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12 or a compiled DIRECT2D; otherwise discovery fails before any test.
concepts.note: Default-only emulator limitation already recorded as WP02-i007/WP19-i001.

concepts.section: CTest must know that PE files are not host executables
concepts.text: Discovery and device-free unit tests run with a narrowly named gate bypass because they cannot print a translator marker, while renderer smoke registrations put the wrapper in their own command without it, since they create a device and must prove engagement.
tokens: Gate bypass set for discovery and unit tests

concepts.section: CTest must know that PE files are not host executables
concepts.text: The strict public-API compile check carries its own emulator wiring for the Direct3D defaults, and per-example registrations keep explicit wrapper commands; GDI's cross-built examples are built but deliberately not registered with CTest.

concepts.section: Native MSVC is a separate lane
concepts.text: Native MSVC is a separate, manual tier (win32-native, d3d-windows-ci, gdi-windows-ci, and a branch-triggered content-pipeline job under a Unicode path); cloud runners do not prove interactive IME, raw devices, multi-monitor, fullscreen or physical-GPU behaviour, so MinGW+Wine, native automation and human Windows use are three tiers.

concepts.section: Native MSVC is a separate lane
concepts.text: The Win32 suite exposed a client-area assertion that silently required a large screen: Windows clamps a client area to the work area, so the same executable passed on a 1920x1080 desktop and failed in session 0 and under Wine's 1024x768 virtual desktop until the tests derived sizes from SPI_GETWORKAREA.

issues.text: GDI's cross-built examples are not registered with CTest in a cross tree; GDI's only automatic CTest route is the manual native workflow.
The MinGW runtime-copy helpers only warn when a runtime DLL cannot be located, so a built tree can fail to start in a clean prefix; a documented design choice, not a defect.
